results.title: Spacecraft Test and Evaluation using Semantic Web Technologies
results.abstract: One area of digital engineering that has received significant attention in recent years is the digital thread. In particular, seamless traceability from requirements through models to simulation results is becoming an increasingly important aspect of this digitalization effort. In this paper, we present an approach to requirements verification that leverages semantic web technologies to support technical and data interoperability with regards to requirements, system architecture, and analysis. The Orbital Verification Ontology Stack (OVOS) is a set of ontologies within the overall University of Arizona Ontology Stack (UAOS) that have been selected to support orbital analysis and requirement verification. The OVOS is written in the Ontological Modeling Language (OML) and is built on the Basic Formal Ontology (BFO) and the Common Core Ontologies (CCO). The Violet tool is used to aggregate data from multiple engineering tools and is able to generate an OML graph representation of entire dataset. This dataset can then be validated against the OVOS and can be reasoned upon and queried by the user. This approach has been applied to a notional LEO spacecraft design project. System-level requirements, the physical architecture of the spacecraft, and an orbital analysis have been captured in different engineering tools. We use Violet to aggregate this data and generate an OML graph presentation of the dataset. We show that semantic web technologies, such as reasoning, validation and querying, have the potential to add value and efficiency to the verification process.

results.title: Spacecraft Configuration Design Exploration Through Transformer-Based Reinforcement Learning
results.abstract: Configuration design, or the placement and orienting of components in a system, is an essential aspect of the engineering design process for many systems, and choices made in this stage can have a large downstream impact on cost and performance. Spacecraft are one such system, with many components that must be placed according to competing goals and requirements. Due to the complex and multi-domain nature of the problem, spacecraft configuration design currently relies heavily on the intuition and experience of a team of engineers. The problem addressed is, given a list of components and their characteristics (mass, dimensions, type, etc.), produce locations and orientations for each component which optimize on some given objectives. To solve this, a transformer model trained using a deep reinforcement learning (deep RL) implementation, Proximal Policy Optimization, is used. The transformer is benchmarked against a multi-objective genetic algorithm, NSGA-II, and random search. Results show the transformer model expands the Pareto front significantly more quickly than the genetic algorithm and the random search. This method could be used by spacecraft design teams to quickly perform a thorough tradespace exploration of the configuration design space. Additionally, with an appropriate set of components and objective and constraint functions, this method could be applied to other configuration design problems, such as chiplet design.

results.title: AI-Enhanced Digital Twin Modeling for Spacecraft Power Systems
results.abstract: The Electrical Power Systems (EPS) is a key subsystem of spacecrafts. It is essential to perform spacecraft power system experiments to verify the performance, stability and fault response capability of the power system. However, ground testing of real spacecraft power system takes a long time and consumes a large amount of human and material resources. Establishing a digital twin model of the power system is crucial for the optimal design of power-system faults responses, real-time state monitoring, and improving operation efficiency. However, the current digital twin models have problems of periodic cumulative error and numerical distortion in simulation. This work proposes a lightweight digital-twin alignment pipeline that keeps an EPS simulator numerically consistent with telemetry over long windows (thousands of seconds) without modifying the flight-validated physics model. Through experimental verification, for the representative EPS telemetry series, the solar array bus-voltage periodic error can be reduced from ±3.2% to ±0.7%, and mean load-power bias has decreased from 42 W to 8 W.

results.title: Designing Modular Spacecraft Power Systems for Radiation, Thermal, and Mechanical Reliability
results.abstract: Two of the most important reliability considerations for spacecraft electronics are radiation degradation, and thermomechanical degradation caused by thermal cycling. High-energy ion flux, electromagnetic radiation, and secondary radiation effects degrade semiconductor components and insulating materials, leading to parametric shifts, performance degradation, and potential failure, while thermomechanical cycling can cause failure via fatigue and is arguably the most common failure mechanism encountered in electronics. This study focuses on the reliability of a radiation-hardened power module by performing targeted materials and electronics irradiation testing in addition to conventional thermal cycling tests to assess probability of survival and long-term performance degradation under the mission profiles identified. The primary objective is to ensure adequate system performance by developing statistical models that predict degradation and failure probabilities based on experimental data. In addition, separate thermal cycling reliability estimations will be developed based on thermal cycling simulations. The thermal cycling model will involve designing and modeling the module layout to optimize thermal isolation and structural integrity while maintaining a compact footprint. The material stack-up, including interconnects and thermal interfaces, will be evaluated to ensure reliability under extreme temperature ranges. Finite element based thermal cycling simulations will be performed to create and validate appropriate thermal management, identify reliability concerns due to accumulated stress from CTE mismatches during thermal cycling, and locate stress concentrations within the device stack-up. The effect of different material choices and design dimensions on the stresses in the package will be determined. Assembly of preliminary modules will then be carried out to validate the structural design and assess manufacturability. Integrating both models into one comprehensive failure predict ion framework will be explored

results.title: Reliability Improvement Methods for Power Loss in Spacecraft Power Systems
results.abstract: The reliability of spacecraft power systems directly impacts the success or failure of space missions. This paper focuses on a certain type of spacecraft power system, employing fault tree analysis to construct a fault tree model with 'bus power failure' as the top event. Through qualitative analysis, 'no output at bus convergence' is identified as a critical singlepoint fault of order-minimum cut set. Based on this, targeted reliability improvement measures are proposed and implemented from four dimensions: design, manufacturing process, process control, and experimental verification. The research results show that the proposed measures effectively improve system reliability, providing theoretical guidance and engineering reference for the design and optimization of spacecraft power systems.

results.title: A Three-Port DC–DC Converter With Optimal Control Strategy for Spacecraft Power Systems
results.abstract: In spacecraft power systems, a power electronic interface is required to manage the power flow between the photovoltaic (PV) source, battery, and load. In this article, a novel three-port converter with optimal control strategy is proposed for this application. The proposed converter is derived by integrating an interleaved buck/boost circuit (IBBC) and a dual active bridge (DAB) circuit, which eliminates the interaction between IBBC and DAB circuit, and achieves decoupled power control between three ports. The optimal control strategy is customized in different operation modes, which widens the zero-voltage switching range and minimizes the inductor current stress in the transformer. In additional, a minimum competition mechanism is applied to achieve smooth and seamless transitions between different modes, so the control strategy is suitable for wide battery voltage and wide load requirements. Furthermore, the interleaved structure of IBBC reduces the input current ripple. This prolongs the lifetime of the PV panels. Finally, a 500 W prototype has been built to verify the effectiveness of the proposed converter and optimal control strategy. The experimental results are consistent with the theoretical analysis.

results.title: Enhanced multi-objective optimization of spacecraft power systems based on a three-phase hybrid optimization algorithm
results.abstract: Optimizing the configurations of a spacecraft power subsystem (SPSS) with given constraints for cost, mass, and performance is a complex task. This study presents two major contributions. The first contribution of this study is the enhanced discrete water cycle algorithm (DWCA), in which three novel features have been integrated: (i) increased crossover diversity, (ii) similarity-based mutation, and (iii) adaptive penalty function management. The results obtained for the power system design by the improved DWCA and the baseline DWCA were compared. The results obtained by the improved DWCA converged to the optimum value faster and showed better stability than those obtained by the baseline DWCA. Second, a three-phase hybrid search framework for SPSS configuration design space exploration is proposed. The three phases were designed using the improved DWCA, GWO, and ACO methods. The three search methods have their respective advantages, that is, global search, leader-based search, and pheromone optimization, thus enabling the optimal solution and good solution diversity in the design space. The hybrid method produces results at a 30 % faster rate than other methods while achieving Integrated Performance Index (IPI) improvements ranging from 6 % to >70 %. The framework embeds a mission-oriented weighted optimization strategy, and is validated for four design spaces, corresponding to four typical space missions, i.e., LEO communication satellite, deep-space scientific probe, Earth observation satellite, and low-cost CubeSat missions. Improved integrated performance was demonstrated across the four case studies for various design objectives. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables the development of efficient SPSS configurations. In certain instances, the improved DWCA and GWO resulted in better trade-offs between the cost and mass. These results also indicate that the hybrid system remains sensitive to the parameter changes. Despite this limitation, the hybrid solution enables power-oriented missions to benefit from improved IPI performance and design flexibility under constrained operational conditions. This research highlights the advancement of an improved DWCA in combination with a hybrid method for spacecraft subsystem optimization. Future research will investigate adaptive parameter-tuning systems to improve system reliability and maintain stable performance across different mission environments.
